title: Micro-huddle opener — 15m script + hot Q&A backlog
content:
Purpose: 15-minute micro-huddle to sync platform priorities, give one quick metric highlight, surface one risk, ask one concrete help request, and leave 5 minutes for hot questions. This is a tight, focused opener for weekly team syncs or when I drop into an on-call bridge.

Structure (timing in parentheses):
- Welcome + framing (0:00–0:30)
  - "'Thanks all for being here. I know folks are stretched—this is a quick sync to align on one signal, one risk, and one ask. We’ll capture other items in the parking lot.'"
- Signal: snapshot metric (0:30–2:00)
  - Quick metric to mention: average p99 response time across hosted inference for last 60m, and token throughput delta vs baseline.
  - Example line: "P99 across hosted inference in the past hour is 420ms, steady +8% vs our baseline; throughput is +12% driven by a reorder of burst traffic from partner X."
- Risk highlight (2:00–4:00)
  - Known issue or emerging risk (one sentence): e.g., batching queues on GPU pool gamma showing longer tail under 1024 token requests.
  - Example line: "We're seeing queue tail growth on pool gamma for long-context requests — this could push over our latency SLO at 1050 token bursts if the trend keeps up."
- Immediate mitigation + ask (4:00–6:00)
  - Short-term mitigation: throttle set, route small percentages to fallback model, increase autoscale headroom for 10 minutes.
  - Concrete ask to the room: "Can infra-oncall (Ravi) stand by to open a temporary routing tweak if we hit 2% error or p99>600ms? Can product (Noor) pause any non-critical traffic experiments for the next 90m?"
- Quick wins / wins to call out (6:00–8:00)
  - Bullet 1: cache hit rate improvement after the prefix cache tweak rolled last night (+6% for embeddings); shoutouts to Marta for the rollout.
  - Bullet 2: dedupe-ing of duplicate requests in our proxy reduced overall token count for a pilot customer by ~18%.
- Parking-lot & follow-ups (8:00–9:00)
  - Where to capture longer threads: add to the meeting doc and ping #platform-ops.
  - Link to longer incident playbook for gamma pool: confluence:ENG-HUDDLE-2026.
- Q&A (9:00–15:00) — prioritize "hot" questions first

Anticipated questions + suggested answers (short, conversational):
- Q: "Is user-facing latency impacted?"
  A: "Not for most customers — the tail is isolated to a specific GPU pool under long-context heavy bursts. We are routing new 1k+ requests to fallback and watching p99 closely."

- Q: "Could this be caused by the recent quantization rollout?"
  A: "Unlikely — quant rollout touched dedicated pool beta; gamma pool hasn't received that change. We're still confirming with serving-runtime logs but early traces suggest different kernel scheduling behavior at long seq lengths."

- Q: "How long will the temporary routing be in place?"
  A: "Target is until the tail flattens below 500ms p99 for two successive 15-minute windows or until we deploy a targeted mitigation. Plan is to reassess at +30 and +90 minutes."

- Q: "Any customer impact we need to proactively contact?"
  A: "Not yet — no elevated error rates. If we see >1% user error or persistent p99>700ms for 30 minutes, we will escalate and send the technical note to CS and account owners."

Notes to self / presenter cues:
- Keep language concrete and non-alarmist: use numbers, not conjecture.
- If an on-call raises a deep runtime thread, park and schedule a 30-minute postmortem — avoid derailing the huddle.
- Have the short link to the playbook ready in chat (confluence:ENG-HUDDLE-2026) and paste the small chart for p95/p99 from observability.
- If asked for timeline, default to time-boxed mitigations (30/90) not vague promises.

Open items (to action after huddle):
- [ ] Ask release-eng to run a quick profile on kernel selection for gamma pool long context jobs — assign to Marta.
- [ ] Add a canary route in staging to simulate 1k+ token bursts and validate queueing behavior — assign to Ravi.
- [ ] Draft one-paragraph customer communication template if we need proactive outreach — assign to Noor.

Tone and delivery tips:
- Start with "thanks" — people respond better to a calm, appreciative tone.
- Use "we" not "they" when referring to teams (e.g., "we rolled a small cache tweak" vs "platform rolled").
- If someone pushes for deep technical detail, offer to take it offline and call the on-call to capture logs.

Parking lot (notes to keep but not mention unless asked):
- Longer debate on autoscaling cooldown thresholds and how they interact with firehose bursts.
- Potential upstream debate about routing policy: cost vs latency tradeoff when routing to quantized fallback.

Quick reference links (paste in chat during huddle):
- Observability chart: dashboard:platform/p99-latency-last-2h
- Gamma pool playbook: confluence:ENG-HUDDLE-2026
- Current incident ticket: JIRA:OPS-4123
- Slack channel: #platform-ops

End line (closing):
- "Thanks everyone — short follow-up in the doc. If you can briefly react with an emoji to the ask so I know who's on it, that helps. I’ll ping again at +30 mins if anything changes."

Rough transcript prompt to paste in meeting notes after: "Aisha opened with the p99 snapshot (420ms, +8%). Risk: queue tail on gamma for 1k+ requests. Mitigation: temporary routing + increased headroom. Ask: oncall stand by to route if p99>600ms; product pause experiments for 90m. Follow-ups assigned to Marta/Ravi/Noor."

Version history:
- 2026-02-25: initial draft
- 2026-03-10: tightened Q&A and added quick wins lines

(End of doc)
